title: US Voters Face Economic Pressure as Midterm Elections Approach
subtitle: High inflation and rising costs of living are shaping voter opinions just weeks before the polls open.

summary.en: Recent data shows US inflation reached 3.7% in September, the highest level before a midterm election since 1990. High energy prices linked to the war with Iran are the main reason for the increased cost of living. A new poll suggests that many voters feel pessimistic about the economy. Both political parties are struggling to convince voters that they have the right solutions. As the election nears, candidates are focusing heavily on these economic concerns.
summary.zh: 最新數據顯示，美國九月份通貨膨脹率達到百分之三點七，是自一九九○年以來期中選舉前的最高水準。與伊朗戰爭相關的高能源價格是生活成本增加的主因。一份最新民調顯示，許多選民對經濟感到悲觀。兩大政黨皆難以說服選民相信自己擁有正確的解決方案。隨著選舉臨近，候選人正將重心高度集中在這些經濟問題上。

paragraphs.en: With the midterm elections less than three weeks away, the American economy has become the most important issue for voters. According to a new poll by Harris for The Guardian, many people are feeling unhappy with the current economic situation. This includes independent voters, rural residents, and even some members of the Republican Party. The poll found that three-quarters of Americans are worried about a recession—a period when the economy gets smaller and people lose jobs—even though the country is not officially in one.
paragraphs.zh: 距離期中選舉剩下不到三週，美國經濟已成為選民最關心的議題。根據哈里斯民調公司（Harris）為《衛報》（The Guardian）所做的最新調查，許多民眾對目前的經濟狀況感到不滿，這群人包括獨立選民、鄉村居民，甚至部分共和黨員。民調顯示，四分之三的美國人擔心經濟衰退——即經濟萎縮且民眾失業的時期——儘管該國目前尚未正式進入衰退。

paragraphs.en: Recent government reports from the Labor Department show that inflation reached 3.7% in September. This is the highest level seen before a midterm election since 1990, if we do not count the pandemic years. Much of this pressure comes from high energy prices, which have risen significantly since the start of the war with Iran. NPR reports that these energy costs are a major factor in the overall increase in the cost of living. For many Americans, this means paying much more at the gas station and the grocery store.
paragraphs.zh: 勞工部（Labor Department）近期的政府報告顯示，九月份通貨膨脹率達到百分之三點七。若不計入疫情期間，這是自一九九○年以來，期中選舉前所見的最高水準。這股壓力很大一部分來自高昂的能源價格，自與伊朗的戰爭爆發以來，能源價格已大幅上漲。美國國家公共電台（NPR）報導指出，這些能源成本是整體生活開銷增加的主要因素。對許多美國人而言，這意味著在加油站和雜貨店必須支付更多費用。

paragraphs.en: In some parts of the country, the situation is even more difficult. Drivers in California are paying an average of $6.20 per gallon of gas, which is $1.20 more than they were paying one year ago. These high prices are changing how people view the political landscape. The poll shows that two-thirds of voters consider gas and grocery prices to be their top concerns, followed by general living expenses, healthcare, and foreign affairs.
paragraphs.zh: 在美國部分地區，情況甚至更加嚴峻。加州的駕駛平均每加侖汽油需支付六點二美元，比一年前多出了一點二美元。這些高昂的價格正在改變民眾對政治局勢的看法。民調顯示，三分之二的選民將油價與食品雜貨價格視為首要關切事項，其次則是整體生活開銷、醫療保健與外交事務。

paragraphs.en: Political candidates are reacting to this frustration by making the economy the center of their campaigns. In Texas, Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico has used campaign videos to show the difficulty of buying basic groceries. Meanwhile, in Michigan, candidate Abdul El-Sayed has spoken to voters about the reality of high gas prices. However, the poll suggests that voters are still divided on which party can actually fix these problems. While 71% of Democrats believe their party has a solution, only 59% of Republicans feel the same about their own party.
paragraphs.zh: 政治候選人正針對這股挫折感做出回應，將經濟議題作為競選活動的核心。在德州，民主黨參議院候選人塔拉里科（James Talarico）透過競選影片展示購買基本雜貨的困難；與此同時，在密西根州，候選人艾爾薩耶德（Abdul El-Sayed）則向選民談論高油價的現實。然而，民調顯示選民對於哪個政黨能真正解決這些問題仍存在分歧。雖然百分之七十一的民主黨人相信自己的政黨有解決方案，但僅有百分之五十九的共和黨人對自己的政黨抱持同樣看法。

paragraphs.en: There is also a growing sense of doubt among voters. Half of all independent voters told pollsters that neither party has a good plan to improve the economy. This feeling is even stronger among rural Americans, who have traditionally been a core group of supporters for President Trump. About 41% of rural voters said they do not believe either party has the right answer. This lack of confidence highlights how difficult it is for politicians to gain trust when people are struggling to pay their bills.
paragraphs.zh: 選民之間也出現了日益增長的懷疑感。半數的獨立選民告訴民調人員，沒有任何政黨有好的計畫來改善經濟。這種感受在鄉村地區的美國人中更為強烈，他們傳統上是川普（Donald Trump）總統的核心支持群體。約百分之四十一的鄉村選民表示，他們不相信任何一方有正確的答案。這種信心的缺乏凸顯出，當民眾難以支付帳單時，政治人物要贏得信任是多麼困難。

paragraphs.en: In response to the rising cost of living, the Social Security Administration recently announced a 3.6% increase in benefits for next year. This is known as a cost-of-living adjustment, which is a change made to payments to help people keep up with higher prices. However, NPR reports that some people who receive these benefits say the increase is not enough to cover their actual expenses. This news comes as the government also warns that the Social Security program might run out of money to pay full benefits to retirees by 2032.
paragraphs.zh: 為了應對生活成本上漲，社會安全署（Social Security Administration）近期宣布明年的福利金將調升百分之三點六。這被稱為生活成本調整，是為了協助民眾跟上物價上漲而對給付金額所做的變動。然而，NPR 報導指出，一些領取這些福利的人士表示，增加的金額不足以支付他們的實際開銷。此消息傳出之際，政府也警告社會安全計畫的資金可能在二○三二年耗盡，屆時將無法支付退休人員的全額福利。

paragraphs.en: As the election date gets closer, the political battle is becoming more intense. Republicans are working hard to keep control of Congress, but they are losing some support among independent voters. At the same time, Democrats are trying to frame the election as a fight against an affordability crisis. The outcome of these races will likely depend on which party can better address the daily financial worries of the American public. With voters feeling that the economy is getting worse, the pressure on all candidates to provide clear, effective solutions will only continue to grow.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著選舉日逼近，政治角力變得更加激烈。共和黨人正努力維持對國會的控制權，但他們在獨立選民中的支持度正在流失。與此同時，民主黨人試圖將這場選舉定調為對抗負擔能力危機的戰役。這些選戰的結果很可能取決於哪個政黨能更好地解決美國大眾日常的財務憂慮。由於選民認為經濟正在惡化，所有候選人面臨提供明確且有效解決方案的壓力只會持續增加。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To include someone or something when calculating a total.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（計數），這裡作動詞表示將某事物納入統計。文中：This is the highest level seen before a midterm election since 1990, if we do not count the pandemic years.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To have no more of something left.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語由動詞與介系詞組成，意思與字面拆解不同。文中：This news comes as the government also warns that the Social Security program might run out of money to pay full benefits to retirees by 2032.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To present or describe a situation in a particular way to influence how people perceive it.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 將某事描述為……；構建……的觀點。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（框架），這裡作動詞表示政治上的論述策略。文中：At the same time, Democrats are trying to frame the election as a fight against an affordability crisis.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the specific reason cited for the recent rise in energy prices?

options.A: The upcoming midterm elections in the United States.
options.C: The Social Security Administration's recent policy changes.
options.D: A global decrease in the production of groceries.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，文中明確提到「Much of this pressure comes from high energy prices, which have risen significantly since the start of the war with Iran.」選項 A 是選舉背景但非能源漲價原因；選項 C 的社會福利調整是為了應對物價，而非漲價原因；選項 D 為無關敘述。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the political climate for the upcoming midterm elections based on the poll results?

options.A: Voters are highly confident that the Republican Party has a clear solution to the economic crisis.
options.B: Independent voters are firmly committed to supporting the Democratic Party to solve inflation.
options.C: There is a widespread lack of faith in both major political parties regarding their economic plans.
options.D: Rural voters are more optimistic about the economy than urban voters due to their support for Trump.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第五段，提到半數獨立選民認為兩黨都沒有好的經濟計畫，且鄉村選民也有 41% 對兩黨皆缺乏信心，這顯示選民對兩黨解決經濟問題的能力普遍存疑。選項 A 與 B 與文中提到的選民分裂及不信任感矛盾；選項 D 文中並未比較鄉村與城市選民的樂觀程度，且提到鄉村選民對兩黨皆感到失望。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'frame' mean as it is used in the phrase 'Democrats are trying to frame the election as a fight against an affordability crisis'?

options.A: To build a physical structure for a building.
options.B: To present or describe a situation in a particular way.
options.C: To falsely accuse someone of a crime they did not commit.
options.D: To change the official rules of an election process.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境下，「frame」意指「將某事界定或塑造成某種觀點」，即民主黨試圖將選舉的主軸定義為對抗負擔能力危機的鬥爭。選項 A 為名詞用法（框架）；選項 C 為負面用法（陷害）；選項 D 則與選舉規則修改無關，皆非文中含義。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the American economy and the midterm elections?

options.A: The government has successfully solved the inflation crisis through Social Security adjustments.
options.B: The midterm elections will be decided solely by voters in California and Texas.
options.C: Voters are frustrated by economic struggles, making the economy the central and uncertain focus of the elections.
options.D: The Republican Party is guaranteed to win because independent voters are unhappy with the current administration.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文核心在於探討經濟問題如何成為選民最關心的議題，並導致選民對兩黨解決方案感到懷疑與焦慮，這使得經濟成為選舉的關鍵變數。選項 A 過於樂觀且與文意不符；選項 B 僅提到部分州，以偏概全；選項 D 錯誤，因為文中提到共和黨也面臨選民支持流失的困境，並非保證勝選。
